children: Real wages in Slovakia fell by 0.5% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, ending ten consecutive quarters of growth and marking the first decline since Q3 2023.
The average nominal monthly wage increased by 3.2% to EUR 1,707, up EUR 53 from a year earlier, but the increase was not enough to offset inflation.
Nominal wages rose in 16 of the 19 monitored sectors, led by real estate activities (9.8%), while public administration recorded the steepest decline (-4.8%).
Real wages increased in 12 sectors, with the strongest gain in real estate (5.9%), while public administration posted the largest drop (-8.2%).
In industry, nominal wages rose 4.9% to EUR 1,878, with real wages up 1.2%, while trade wages increased 4% to EUR 1,596, with real wages gaining 0.3%.
For the first half of 2026, average nominal monthly wages increased 4.6% to EUR 1,659, while real wages rose 0.9%.

title: Slovakia Real Wage Growth Fall in Q2
